# Sage Business Cloud Accounting (South Africa) - Comprehensive Feature Analysis

> **Purpose:** Competitive comparison reference document for ISAFlow
> **Product:** Sage Business Cloud Accounting (formerly Sage One / Sage 0)
> **Region:** South Africa (en-za)
> **Last Updated:** 2026-04-05

---

## Pricing Tiers (ZAR, incl. VAT)

| Plan | Price | Users | Target |
|------|-------|-------|--------|
| **Accounting Start** | From R240/month | 1 user | Sole traders, freelancers, micro-businesses |
| **Accounting Standard** | From R435/month | 2 users (up to 5) | Growing small businesses |
| **Add-on: Multi-Currency** | ~R165/month | - | Foreign currency transactions |
| **Add-on: Time Tracking** | R165/month | - | Project billing, hourly tracking |
| **Add-on: Advanced Inventory** | ~R165/month | - | Warehouse/stock management |
| **Add-on: Debtors Manager** | ~R165/month | - | Collections automation |
| **Sage Payroll** | Separate subscription | Per company | Payroll processing |

> Additional users can be added to Standard for an extra fee per user.

---

## 1. Dashboard & Overview

| Feature | Available | Tier | Notes |
|---------|-----------|------|-------|
| Financial dashboard | Yes | All | Visual money in/out per month |
| Cash position widget | Yes | All | Real-time bank balance display |
| Outstanding invoices widget | Yes | All | Total owed by customers |
| Bills to pay widget | Yes | All | Total owed to suppliers |
| Profit & Loss summary | Yes | All | Current period P&L snapshot |
| Cash flow forecast chart | Yes | Standard | Visual forecast of future cash |
| Bank account balances | Yes | All | Connected bank accounts shown |
| Overdue invoices alert | Yes | All | Highlights overdue amounts |
| Customisable dashboard | Partial | All | Limited widget arrangement; not drag-and-drop customisable like Xero |
| KPI tiles/ratios | No | - | No gross margin %, current ratio, etc. on dashboard |
| Multi-company dashboard | No | - | Single company per login (no group overview) |

**Limitations:** Dashboard is functional but basic compared to competitors. No custom KPI widgets, no configurable date ranges on dashboard widgets, no sparkline trends.

---

## 2. Chart of Accounts / General Ledger

| Feature | Available | Tier | Notes |
|---------|-----------|------|-------|
| Default chart of accounts | Yes | All | Pre-configured ZA-specific COA |
| Custom accounts | Yes | All | Add/edit/deactivate accounts |
| Account categories | Yes | All | Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Revenue, Expenses, Cost of Sales |
| Sub-accounts | Partial | All | Limited hierarchy; not true multi-level nesting |
| Journal entries | Yes | All | General journals with debit/credit |
| Recurring journals | Yes | Standard | Automated periodic journals |
| Opening balances | Yes | All | Via journal entry or take-on balance fields |
| Import COA from CSV | Yes | All | Bulk upload via CSV template |
| Account numbering | Yes | All | Customisable account codes |
| Lock periods | Yes | All | Prevent posting to closed periods |
| Tax codes per account | Yes | All | Default VAT rate per account |
| Departmental tracking | No | - | No tracking categories/departments (use Sage Intacct for this) |
| Multi-segment COA | No | - | Single-segment only |

**Limitations:** No tracking categories or cost centres. No multi-dimensional reporting. Cannot tag transactions to departments/locations/projects at the GL level (projects are a separate add-on). No account-level notes or attachments.

---

## 3. Customers / Accounts Receivable

| Feature | Available | Tier | Notes |
|---------|-----------|------|-------|
| Customer contacts | Yes | All | Full customer database with contact details |
| Quotes/Estimates | Yes | All | Create, email, PDF |
| Convert quote to invoice | Yes | All | One-click conversion |
| Sales invoices | Yes | All | Professional templates, customisable |
| Pro-forma invoices | Yes | All | Supported |
| Credit notes | Yes | All | Against invoices or standalone |
| Draft invoices | Yes | All | Save as draft before sending |
| Recurring invoices | Yes | Standard | Automated at scheduled intervals; email auto-send or save as draft |
| Batch/quick entry invoices | Yes | Standard | Enter multiple invoices at once via Quick Entries |

## What to build

### 1. API: `pages/api/accounting/customer-merge.ts`
POST body: `{ source_id: string, target_id: string }`

Merge logic (all in a single transaction using withTransaction):
1. Validate both customers belong to `companyId`
2. Re-parent all foreign key references from `source_id` → `target_id`:
   - `customer_invoices.customer_id`
   - `customer_payments.customer_id`
   - `customer_contacts.customer_id`
   - `customer_delivery_addresses.customer_id`
   - `customer_activities.customer_id` (if table exists — catch error gracefully)
3. Soft-delete source customer: `UPDATE customers SET is_active = false, name = name || ' [MERGED]' WHERE id = source_id`
4. Return `{ merged: true, target_id }`

Auth: `withCompany` + `withErrorHandler` + `withWriteAccess`

### 2. API: `pages/api/accounting/customer-duplicates.ts`
GET — Find potential duplicate customers

Query: find customers with similar names (trigram or ILIKE) or same email/VAT:
```sql
SELECT a.id AS id_a, a.name AS name_a, a.email AS email_a,
       b.id AS id_b, b.name AS name_b, b.email AS email_b,
       CASE WHEN a.email IS NOT NULL AND a.email = b.email THEN 'email'
            WHEN a.vat_number IS NOT NULL AND a.vat_number = b.vat_number THEN 'vat'
            ELSE 'name' END AS match_reason
FROM customers a
JOIN customers b ON b.id > a.id
  AND b.company_id = a.company_id
  AND b.is_active = true
WHERE a.company_id = ${companyId}
  AND a.is_active = true
  AND (
    (a.email IS NOT NULL AND a.email = b.email)
    OR (a.vat_number IS NOT NULL AND a.vat_number = b.vat_number)
    OR (a.name ILIKE '%' || split_part(b.name, ' ', 1) || '%' AND length(split_part(b.name, ' ', 1)) > 3)
  )
LIMIT 20
```

-- Adds support for multiple contacts per customer (Sage parity)

  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  customer_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  full_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  role VARCHAR(100),
  email VARCHAR(255),
  phone VARCHAR(50),
  is_primary BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS customer_contacts_customer_id_idx ON customer_contacts(customer_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS customer_contacts_company_id_idx ON customer_contacts(company_id);

Build the multi-currency API layer for ISAFlow (/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow).

The pure service already exists at `src/modules/accounting/services/multiCurrencyService.ts` — read it first to understand the types.

## What to build

### 1. Migration — `scripts/migrations/sql/297_multi_currency.sql`
Check what the next available migration number is first:
```bash
ls scripts/migrations/sql/ | sort | tail -5
```

Create the migration with IF NOT EXISTS guards:
```sql
-- Currencies table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS currencies (
  code        VARCHAR(3) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  symbol      VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
  is_active   BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Seed default currencies
INSERT INTO currencies (code, name, symbol) VALUES
  ('ZAR', 'South African Rand', 'R'),
  ('USD', 'US Dollar', '$'),
  ('EUR', 'Euro', '€'),
  ('GBP', 'British Pound', '£'),
  ('BWP', 'Botswana Pula', 'P'),
  ('ZWL', 'Zimbabwe Dollar', 'Z$'),
  ('NAD', 'Namibian Dollar', 'N$'),
  ('MUR', 'Mauritian Rupee', '₨'),
  ('KES', 'Kenyan Shilling', 'KSh'),
  ('NGN', 'Nigerian Naira', '₦')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

-- Exchange rates table (company-scoped — each company can override rates)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS exchange_rates (
  id             UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  from_currency  VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL REFERENCES currencies(code),
  to_currency    VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL REFERENCES currencies(code),
  rate           NUMERIC(18,6) NOT NULL CHECK (rate > 0),
  effective_date DATE NOT NULL,
  source         VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'manual',
  created_by     UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_exchange_rates_company_pair_date
  ON exchange_rates (company_id, from_currency, to_currency, effective_date);

-- Add functional_currency to companies (base currency, default ZAR)
ALTER TABLE companies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS functional_currency VARCHAR(3) DEFAULT 'ZAR' REFERENCES currencies(code);
```

Apply it:
```bash
npx tsx scripts/run-sql.mjs scripts/migrations/sql/NNN_multi_currency.sql
```

### 2. `pages/api/accounting/currencies.ts` — GET list of currencies
- GET: returns all active currencies from the `currencies` table
- No company_id needed (currencies are global)
- `withCompany(withErrorHandler(handler))` still required (auth check)

### 3. `pages/api/accounting/exchange-rates.ts` — CRUD for exchange rates
- GET: list exchange rates for the company, optional `?fromCurrency=&toCurrency=&date=`
- POST: create a new rate — body: `{ fromCurrency, toCurrency, rate, effectiveDate }`
  - Validate using `validateExchangeRate` from multiCurrencyService
  - INSERT with company_id
- DELETE: `?id=UUID` — delete a specific rate (company-scoped check)
- Use `withWriteAccess` for POST/DELETE

### 4. `pages/api/accounting/exchange-rate-convert.ts` — Convert amounts
- POST: body `{ amount, fromCurrency, toCurrency, date? }`
- Looks up the most recent exchange rate on or before `date` (defaults to today)
- Uses `convertAmount` from multiCurrencyService
- Returns `{ result, rate, effectiveDate }`

## Standards
- `withCompany(withErrorHandler(handler as any))` wrapping
- `withWriteAccess` for mutations
- `sql` tagged templates, company_id on every company-scoped query
- `apiResponse.success/badRequest/notFound`
- `log` from `@/lib/logger`
- Max 300 lines per file

After building, run:
```bash
npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck 2>&1 | grep "error TS" | wc -l
```
Must be 0.

Report what was built and file paths.

tool_input.prompt:
Build the multi-currency UI pages for ISAFlow (/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow).

The pure service is at `src/modules/accounting/services/multiCurrencyService.ts` — read it for types like `formatCurrencyAmount`.

APIs (being built concurrently — assume they exist):
- GET `/api/accounting/currencies` → `{ data: { currencies: Array<{code, name, symbol}> } }`
- GET `/api/accounting/exchange-rates` → `{ data: { rates: Array<{id, fromCurrency, toCurrency, rate, effectiveDate}> } }`
- POST `/api/accounting/exchange-rates` body: `{ fromCurrency, toCurrency, rate, effectiveDate }`
- DELETE `/api/accounting/exchange-rates?id=UUID`
- POST `/api/accounting/exchange-rate-convert` body: `{ amount, fromCurrency, toCurrency, date? }` → `{ data: { result, rate, effectiveDate } }`

## Page 1: `pages/accounting/settings/exchange-rates.tsx`

Exchange rate management page:
- Page header: "Exchange Rates" with subtitle "Manage foreign currency exchange rates"
- **Current rates table**: columns — From, To, Rate, Effective Date, Actions (Delete button)
  - Show rates grouped or sorted by from_currency
  - Format rate to 6 decimal places
- **Add Rate form** (inline, above the table or in a card):
  - From Currency: dropdown (loaded from `/api/accounting/currencies`)
  - To Currency: dropdown
  - Rate: number input (placeholder "e.g. 18.523400")
  - Effective Date: date input (default today)
  - "Add Rate" button → POST then refresh list
- **Currency Converter widget** (small card, sidebar or bottom):
  - Amount input, From/To currency dropdowns, Date input
  - "Convert" button → POST to exchange-rate-convert
  - Shows result: "R 1,000.00 = $ 54.05 (rate: 0.054050 on 2026-04-11)"
- Loading states, error handling, success toasts (use existing toast pattern if any, otherwise simple inline green text)

## Page 2: `pages/accounting/settings/currencies.tsx`

Simple read-only currencies reference page:
- Table of all currencies: Code, Name, Symbol
- Can be a simple static-ish page (loads from `/api/accounting/currencies`)
- Title: "Supported Currencies"

## Nav registration

Add to `src/components/accounting/navSections/` — check the settings nav file (look for `settings.ts` or similar). Add:
- "Exchange Rates" → `/accounting/settings/exchange-rates`  
- "Currencies" → `/accounting/settings/currencies`

If no settings nav section exists, add to the most appropriate existing section (e.g. `generalLedger.ts` or create `settings.ts`).

## Standards
- `AppLayout` wrapper on all pages
- `apiFetch` — never raw fetch
- ISAFlow design tokens: `var(--ff-bg-primary)`, `var(--ff-text-primary)`, `var(--ff-border-light)`, teal-500 for primary actions
- Tailwind for all styling
- `useCallback` + `useEffect` for data loading
- Currency formatting: use `formatCurrencyAmount` from the service where appropriate
- Max 300 lines per file — split into 2 files if needed
- No `console.log`
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck 2>&1 | grep "error TS" | wc -l` after each file

Report what was built and file paths.

VALUES
  (gen_random_uuid(), 'ZAR', 'South African Rand',  'R',   true,  true, 2),
  (gen_random_uuid(), 'USD', 'US Dollar',            '$',   false, true, 2),
  (gen_random_uuid(), 'EUR', 'Euro',                 '€',   false, true, 2),
  (gen_random_uuid(), 'GBP', 'British Pound',        '£',   false, true, 2),

  (gen_random_uuid(), 'MUR', 'Mauritian Rupee',      '₨',   false, true, 2),
  (gen_random_uuid(), 'KES', 'Kenyan Shilling',      'KSh', false, true, 2),

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

ALTER TABLE exchange_rates ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source     VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'manual';
ALTER TABLE exchange_rates ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS created_by UUID REFERENCES users(id);

-- Unique index to support ON CONFLICT in setExchangeRate()
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_exchange_rates_company_pair_date

-- ── 3. companies: add functional_currency ────────────────────────────────────
-- The table already has default_currency (text). We add functional_currency as

ALTER TABLE companies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS functional_currency VARCHAR(3) DEFAULT 'ZAR';

-- Migration 297: Multi-currency support
-- Fills gaps in currencies / exchange_rates tables and seeds global currencies.
-- All DDL uses IF NOT EXISTS / ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS guards.

-- ── 1. currencies: relax company_id to allow global (system) currency rows ───

ALTER TABLE currencies ALTER COLUMN company_id DROP NOT NULL;

-- Add decimal_places if missing
ALTER TABLE currencies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS decimal_places INTEGER DEFAULT 2;

-- Seed global (non-company-scoped) currency rows
INSERT INTO currencies (code, name, symbol, is_base, is_active, decimal_places)
VALUES
  ('ZAR', 'South African Rand',  'R',   true,  true, 2),
  ('USD', 'US Dollar',            '$',   false, true, 2),
  ('EUR', 'Euro',                 '€',   false, true, 2),
  ('GBP', 'British Pound',        '£',   false, true, 2),
  ('BWP', 'Botswana Pula',        'P',   false, true, 2),
  ('ZWL', 'Zimbabwe Dollar',      'Z$',  false, true, 2),
  ('NAD', 'Namibian Dollar',      'N$',  false, true, 2),
  ('MUR', 'Mauritian Rupee',      '₨',   false, true, 2),
  ('KES', 'Kenyan Shilling',      'KSh', false, true, 2),
  ('NGN', 'Nigerian Naira',       '₦',   false, true, 2)
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

-- ── 2. exchange_rates: add missing columns ────────────────────────────────────

ALTER TABLE exchange_rates ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source     VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'manual';
ALTER TABLE exchange_rates ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS created_by UUID REFERENCES users(id);

-- Unique index to support ON CONFLICT in setExchangeRate()
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_exchange_rates_company_pair_date
  ON exchange_rates (company_id, from_currency, to_currency, effective_date);

-- ── 3. companies: add functional_currency ────────────────────────────────────

ALTER TABLE companies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS functional_currency VARCHAR(3) DEFAULT 'ZAR';

- `pages/accounting/customer-sales-orders/index.tsx` — SO list page (has status badges, needs action buttons)
- `pages/api/accounting/customer-sales-orders.ts` — SO API (needs a convert action)
- `pages/api/accounting/customer-invoices-create.ts` — Invoice create API (understand the invoice creation pattern)
- `pages/api/accounting/customer-quotes-action.ts` — Quote action pattern (convert-to-SO already exists here — mirror this pattern for SO-to-invoice)

## What to build

### 1. API action: add `convert` to `pages/api/accounting/customer-sales-orders.ts`
Add a POST handler for `action=convert`:
- Body: `{ id: string, line_ids?: string[] }` (line_ids = partial invoicing, empty = all lines)
- Fetch the SO and its lines (with company_id scope)
- Validate SO status is `confirmed` or `partially_invoiced`
- Create a new customer invoice from the SO data:
  - Copy: customer_id, reference (SO number as ref), due_date (from SO if exists, else payment terms), notes
  - For each SO line (or selected lines): copy item_id, description, quantity, unit_price, vat_rate, discount
  - Set invoice status = `draft`
  - Insert into `customer_invoices` + `customer_invoice_lines` (use the same pattern as `customer-invoices-create.ts`)
- Update SO status:
  - If all lines invoiced → `invoiced`
  - Else → `partially_invoiced`
  - Set `invoiced_at = NOW()` and `invoice_id = <new invoice id>`
- Return `{ invoice_id, invoice_number }`
- Use `withTransaction` for atomicity
- Auth: `withCompany` + `withErrorHandler` + `withWriteAccess`

### 2. UI: add "Create Invoice" button to SO list in `pages/accounting/customer-sales-orders/index.tsx`
Read the file first, then:
- On rows where status is `confirmed` or `partially_invoiced`: show a "Create Invoice" button (FileText icon, small, in an actions column or inline)
- On click: POST to `/api/accounting/customer-sales-orders` with `action=convert`, then:
  - Navigate to `/accounting/customer-invoices/${invoice_id}` (or show success toast with link)
- Show loading state on the button while converting
- Handle errors with an inline error message

## Requirements
- Full TypeScript, no `any`
- company_id scoping on all DB queries
- Use `withTransaction` for the convert operation
- No console.log — use `log.info`/`log.error` from `@/lib/logger`
- Match existing page styling

tool_input.prompt:
Build Customer Transaction Ledger and Supplier Transaction Ledger reports for ISAFlow. Working directory: /home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow.

## Context — read these files first:
- `pages/accounting/reports/customer-reports.tsx` — existing customer report (understand the page structure/style)
- `pages/api/accounting/reports-customer.ts` — customer report API (understand the query pattern)
- `pages/accounting/reports/supplier-reports.tsx` — existing supplier report
- `pages/accounting/reports/` — list all files to understand naming convention

## What to build

### 1. API: `pages/api/accounting/reports-customer-ledger.ts`
GET params: `customerId` (required), `dateFrom?`, `dateTo?`

Query — union of all customer transactions ordered by date:
```sql
SELECT
  'invoice'        AS type,
  ci.id            AS transaction_id,
  ci.invoice_number AS reference,
  ci.invoice_date  AS transaction_date,
  ci.total_amount  AS debit,
  0                AS credit,
  ci.status
FROM customer_invoices ci
WHERE ci.company_id = ${companyId} AND ci.customer_id = ${customerId}
  AND (${dateFrom}::date IS NULL OR ci.invoice_date >= ${dateFrom})
  AND (${dateTo}::date IS NULL OR ci.invoice_date <= ${dateTo})

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'receipt'        AS type,
  cp.id            AS transaction_id,
  cp.reference     AS reference,
  cp.payment_date  AS transaction_date,
  0                AS debit,
  cp.amount        AS credit,
  'paid'           AS status
FROM customer_payments cp
WHERE cp.company_id = ${companyId} AND cp.customer_id = ${customerId}
  AND (${dateFrom}::date IS NULL OR cp.payment_date >= ${dateFrom})
  AND (${dateTo}::date IS NULL OR cp.payment_date <= ${dateTo})

ORDER BY transaction_date ASC, type ASC
```

Compute running balance (debit - credit accumulated). Return: `{ customer_name, transactions: [...], opening_balance, closing_balance }`.

Auth: `withCompany` + `withErrorHandler`

- Export CSV button

### 4. Page: `pages/accounting/reports/supplier-ledger.tsx`
Mirror of customer ledger but for suppliers.

### 5. Add to nav

## What to build

### 1. API: `pages/api/accounting/reports-customer-ledger.ts`
GET params: `customerId` (required), `dateFrom?`, `dateTo?`

Query — union of all customer transactions ordered by date:
```sql
SELECT
  'invoice'        AS type,
  ci.id            AS transaction_id,
  ci.invoice_number AS reference,
  ci.invoice_date  AS transaction_date,
  ci.total_amount  AS debit,
  0                AS credit,
  ci.status
FROM customer_invoices ci
WHERE ci.company_id = ${companyId} AND ci.customer_id = ${customerId}
  AND (${dateFrom}::date IS NULL OR ci.invoice_date >= ${dateFrom})
  AND (${dateTo}::date IS NULL OR ci.invoice_date <= ${dateTo})

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'receipt'        AS type,
  cp.id            AS transaction_id,
  cp.reference     AS reference,
  cp.payment_date  AS transaction_date,
  0                AS debit,
  cp.amount        AS credit,
  'paid'           AS status
FROM customer_payments cp
WHERE cp.company_id = ${companyId} AND cp.customer_id = ${customerId}
  AND (${dateFrom}::date IS NULL OR cp.payment_date >= ${dateFrom})
  AND (${dateTo}::date IS NULL OR cp.payment_date <= ${dateTo})

ORDER BY transaction_date ASC, type ASC
```

Compute running balance (debit - credit accumulated). Return: `{ customer_name, transactions: [...], opening_balance, closing_balance }`.

Auth: `withCompany` + `withErrorHandler`

Mirror of customer ledger but for suppliers.

The `cspProd` script-src is `'self'` only — does NOT include `https://static.cloudflareinsights.com`. **BUG-005 is NOT fixed** in the local code either. The fix would need to add `https://static.cloudflareinsights.com` to the `script-src` directive.

Now I have all the information needed for a comprehensive report.

---

## QA Report: Admin Platform Bug Fixes
Date: 2026-04-11

**Testing environment note:** `localhost:3200` middleware redirects all `/admin/*` routes to `https://admin.isaflow.co.za` (production). Testing was conducted against the production admin platform. The local codebase was also inspected for all fixes.

| Step | Bug | Action | Expected | Actual | Result |
|------|-----|--------|----------|--------|--------|
| 1 | BUG-001 | Navigate to `/billing/overview` (authenticated) | Redirect to `/billing` | **404 Not Found** — no redirect page exists | **FAIL** |
| 2 | BUG-003 | View `/companies` list | "Add Company" button top-right + modal with fields | No "Add Company" button visible; no modal | **FAIL** |
| 3 | BUG-004 | View `/companies` list row | Actions column with Impersonate + Suspend icon buttons | No Actions column; table ends at "Last Active" | **FAIL** |
| 4 | BUG-005 | Check browser console on admin page | No Cloudflare beacon CSP violation | `script-src 'self'` violation for `static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js` still present | **FAIL** |
| 5 | BUG-006 | Navigate to `/analytics` | "Platform Summary" section with Companies/Users/Invoices/JE/Bank Txn/DB size stats | Page shows "Usage Analytics" with DAU/WAU/MAU only — **no Platform Summary section** | **FAIL** |
| 6 | BUG-007 | Click company → detail page tabs | Three tabs: Info, Users, **Features** | Only two tabs: Info, Users — **no Features tab** | **FAIL** |

**Summary: 0/6 steps passed**

---

### Root Cause Analysis

All 6 fixes are absent from both production and the local dev codebase. Specific findings per bug:

**BUG-001** — `/pages/admin/billing/overview.tsx` does not exist. Fix requires either creating the page with a `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` redirect, or adding a `redirect` in `next.config.js`/`_middleware`.

**BUG-003** — `pages/admin/companies/index.tsx` has no "Add Company" button or create modal code (237 lines total, no `setShowCreate`, no form modal). Fix requires adding the button and modal.

**BUG-004** — `companies/index.tsx` table rows only render 7 data columns with no Actions column. `handleImpersonate` and `UserCog`/`ShieldOff` icons exist only on the detail page `[id].tsx`, not the list. Fix requires adding an 8th Actions column to the list table.

**BUG-005** — `next.config.js` `cspProd` value is `"script-src 'self'"` — no Cloudflare beacon domain allowed. Fix: add `https://static.cloudflareinsights.com` to `script-src` in production CSP.

**BUG-006** — `pages/admin/analytics.tsx` calls `/api/admin/analytics/usage` only. No `platform_summary` interface, no Platform Summary section in JSX. The `/api/admin/analytics/health` endpoint does return `db_size_mb` and active user counts, but the page doesn't consume it. Fix requires adding a second API call + Platform Summary card grid to the analytics page.

**BUG-007** — `pages/admin/companies/[id].tsx` has `useState<'info' | 'users'>('info')` — only two tab states. No features loading logic, no Features tab button, no Features tab panel. Fix requires adding `'features'` to the tab union type and implementing the tab panel using the existing `/api/admin/companies/[id]/features` endpoint (which works and returns data correctly).

---

### Additional Regressions / Observations

1. **Company detail page action buttons**: Impersonate, Suspend, Export Data, and Delete buttons ARE present on the company detail page header — these work correctly. The issue (BUG-004) is their absence from the list view.

2. **Sidebar inconsistency**: The Billing section shows sub-nav items (Overview, Plans, Subscriptions, Invoices) only when navigated via login `returnTo` redirect — not when navigating from the main sidebar. This is a minor sidebar state bug unrelated to the 6 bugs above.

3. **Company ISAFlow Demo has no Plan shown**: In the companies table, "ISAFlow Demo (Pty) Ltd" shows no plan name (empty Plan column) — possibly a data issue.

4. **CSP secondary issue**: Form field elements missing `id` or `name` attributes (2 occurrences) — also reported as a browser issue.

5. **`/api/admin/analytics` returns 404** (no index route at that path) — the analytics API only has sub-routes `/analytics/health` and `/analytics/usage`. This is fine if the page only calls the sub-routes, but worth noting for any future direct calls to `/api/admin/analytics`.

Zero TypeScript errors across the entire project. All files are clean.

SUMMARY: Built Customer Transaction Ledger and Supplier Transaction Ledger reports — 2 API routes and 2 pages, with nav wiring.

ANALYSIS: Key schema findings that shaped the implementation:
- `customer_invoices` has both `customer_id` (original) and `client_id` (added in migration 211) — uses `COALESCE(ci.client_id, ci.customer_id)`
- `customer_payments` uses `client_id` (not `customer_id`) and `bank_reference`/`payment_number` for reference
- `supplier_payments` uses `reference`/`payment_number` for reference
- `sql` from `@/lib/neon` does not support generics — uses `as Type[]` casts
- `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` tsconfig flag makes `.split('T')[0]` return `string | undefined` — fixed with `?? raw`

ACTIONS:
- Created `/pages/api/accounting/reports-customer-ledger.ts` — GET with `customerId`, `dateFrom?`, `dateTo?`; UNION of customer_invoices + customer_payments with running balance computation
- Created `/pages/api/accounting/reports-supplier-ledger.ts` — same pattern for supplier_invoices + supplier_payments
- Created `/pages/accounting/reports/customer-ledger.tsx` — lazy-loaded customer dropdown, date range, run-report button, ledger table with colour-coded debit/credit/balance columns, summary strip, CSV export

Two infrastructure improvements for ISAFlow (/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow).

## Task 1: NL Query Performance (target: <2s average, currently 3.9s)

Read `pages/api/accounting/nl-query.ts` and `src/modules/accounting/services/nlQueryService.ts`.

The bottleneck is the Claude AI call. Improve with:

### 1a. System prompt caching
The Anthropic SDK supports prompt caching via `cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }` on large system prompt blocks. Check how the AI call is made (likely via `@anthropic-ai/sdk`). Add `cache_control` to the system prompt message so it's cached between requests:

```typescript
// In the messages array:
{
  role: 'user',
  content: [
    {
      type: 'text',
      text: SYSTEM_PROMPT,  // the large schema/instructions block
      cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' },
    },
    {
      type: 'text', 
      text: userQuestion,
    }
  ]
}
```

### 1b. Reduce system prompt size
Read the current system prompt in `nlQueryService.ts`. Remove any redundant examples or verbose descriptions. Keep only: table schemas, column names, examples, and security rules. Target: under 2000 tokens.

### 1c. Lower temperature + max_tokens
Ensure: `temperature: 0` (SQL generation is deterministic), `max_tokens: 500` (SQL rarely needs more).

### 1d. Add response caching for identical questions
In `nl-query.ts`, add a simple in-memory LRU cache (max 100 entries) keyed by `companyId + question`. Use a Map with LRU eviction (oldest entry deleted when size > 100). Cache TTL: 5 minutes. If cache hit, skip the AI call entirely.

```typescript
// Simple LRU Map cache at module level:
const queryCache = new Map<string, { result: NlQueryResult; ts: number }>();
const CACHE_TTL = 5 * 60 * 1000;
const CACHE_MAX = 100;
```

## Task 2: API Rate Limiting

Add per-company rate limiting to prevent abuse. Use an in-memory sliding window approach (no Redis needed).

Create `src/lib/rateLimiter.ts`:
```typescript
// Sliding window rate limiter
// Default: 100 requests per minute per company
export function checkRateLimit(companyId: string, limit = 100, windowMs = 60_000): { allowed: boolean; remaining: number; resetMs: number }
```

Apply to the most abuse-prone endpoints by adding a check at the top of the handler:

1. `pages/api/accounting/nl-query.ts` — limit: 20/min (AI calls are expensive)
2. `pages/api/accounting/smart-categorize.ts` — limit: 30/min
3. `pages/api/accounting/customer-invoices.ts` — limit: 60/min (write operations)

When rate limit exceeded, return:
```typescript
return res.status(429).json({ success: false, error: 'Rate limit exceeded', retryAfter: Math.ceil(resetMs / 1000) });
```

- TypeScript strict, no `any`

-- Payroll Module Migration
-- SA Payroll with SARS tax tables, UIF, SDL support

-- ── Employees ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS employees (
  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  employee_number VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  first_name    VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  last_name     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  id_number     VARCHAR(13),
  tax_number    VARCHAR(20),
  start_date    DATE NOT NULL,
  termination_date DATE,
  bank_name     VARCHAR(100),
  bank_account_number VARCHAR(30),
  bank_branch_code VARCHAR(10),
  department    VARCHAR(100),
  position      VARCHAR(100),
  employment_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'permanent'
    CHECK (employment_type IN ('permanent', 'contract', 'temporary')),
  pay_frequency VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'monthly'
    CHECK (pay_frequency IN ('monthly', 'weekly')),
  status        VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'inactive')),
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_employees_status ON employees (status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_employees_employee_number ON employees (employee_number);

-- ── Pay Structures ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pay_structures (
  id                          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  employee_id                 UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES employees(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  basic_salary                NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  travel_allowance            NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  housing_allowance           NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cell_allowance              NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  other_allowances            NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  medical_aid_contribution    NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  retirement_fund_contribution_pct NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  custom_deductions           JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::JSONB,
  effective_from              DATE NOT NULL,
  effective_to                DATE,
  created_at                  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pay_structures_employee ON pay_structures (employee_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pay_structures_effective ON pay_structures (effective_from, effective_to);

-- ── Payroll Runs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS payroll_runs (
  id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  period_start        DATE NOT NULL,
  period_end          DATE NOT NULL,
  run_date            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  status              VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
    CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'processing', 'completed', 'reversed')),
  total_gross         NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_paye          NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_uif_employee  NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_uif_employer  NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_sdl           NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_net           NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_company_cost  NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  journal_entry_id    UUID,
  created_by          UUID,
  created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_payroll_runs_status ON payroll_runs (status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_payroll_runs_period ON payroll_runs (period_start, period_end);

-- ── Payslips ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS payslips (
  id                UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  payroll_run_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES payroll_runs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  employee_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES employees(id),
  basic_salary      NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  travel_allowance  NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  housing_allowance NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cell_allowance    NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  other_allowances  NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  gross_pay         NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  paye              NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  uif_employee      NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  uif_employer      NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  sdl               NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  medical_aid       NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  retirement_fund   NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  other_deductions  NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_deductions  NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  net_pay           NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ytd_gross         NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ytd_paye          NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ytd_uif           NUMERIC(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_payslips_run ON payslips (payroll_run_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_payslips_employee ON payslips (employee_id);

tool_input.description: Customer portal: self-service invoice view and payment link
tool_input.prompt:
Build a customer-facing self-service portal for ISAFlow (/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow).

The portal lets customers view their invoices and pay online via a secure token-based link — no login required.

## Step 1: Check existing infrastructure
```bash
ls pages/portal/ 2>/dev/null || echo "no portal dir"
ls pages/api/portal/ 2>/dev/null || echo "no portal API"
grep -r "portal_token\|portal_link\|customer_portal" scripts/migrations/sql/ --include="*.sql" -l
```

## Step 2: Migration (check next number first with `ls scripts/migrations/sql/ | sort | tail -5`)

```sql
-- Add portal token to invoices for secure shareable links
ALTER TABLE customer_invoices 
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS portal_token VARCHAR(64) UNIQUE,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS portal_viewed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS portal_paid_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_customer_invoices_portal_token 
  ON customer_invoices(portal_token) WHERE portal_token IS NOT NULL;
```

Apply it with `npx tsx scripts/run-sql.mjs`.

## Step 3: Portal API (no auth required — token-based)

### `pages/api/portal/invoice/[token].ts`
- GET: fetch invoice by `portal_token`, return safe fields only (NO internal IDs beyond what's needed, NO company internals)
  - Returns: invoice number, date, due date, line items, subtotal, VAT, total, currency, company name/logo, customer name, status
  - Also updates `portal_viewed_at = NOW()` on first view
  - 404 if token not found or invoice is cancelled
- This route does NOT use `withCompany` (it's public) but DOES validate the token exists

### `pages/api/portal/invoice/[token]/generate-token.ts` (internal — needs auth)
OR better: add `?action=generate-portal-link` to existing invoice detail API
- Generates a random 32-byte hex token, stores it on the invoice, returns the full portal URL

## Step 4: Portal Page (public — no AppLayout)

### `pages/portal/invoice/[token].tsx`
Clean, professional invoice view page (no ISAFlow nav — just the invoice):
- Company logo/name at top
- Invoice number, date, due date
- "OVERDUE" badge if past due date
- Line items table: description, qty, unit price, VAT, total
- Totals: subtotal, VAT, grand total (formatted in invoice currency)
- Status badge: Draft / Sent / Paid / Overdue
- "Pay Now" button (placeholder — opens a modal saying "Contact us to arrange payment")
- "Download PDF" link → links to existing PDF endpoint if available
- Simple clean design with Tailwind — white background, professional typography, ISAFlow branding

## Step 5: Wire "Send Portal Link" into invoice detail
Find `pages/accounting/customer-invoices/[invoiceId].tsx`, read it, add:
- "Copy Portal Link" button that calls generate-token and copies the URL to clipboard
- Shows the portal URL in a read-only input once generated

## Standards
- Portal page: no AppLayout, no auth middleware — fully public
- Use `getServerSideProps` for the portal page to fetch invoice server-side (SEO + no flash)
- API: validate token exists and invoice is not cancelled/deleted
- Max 300 lines per file
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck 2>&1 | grep "error TS" | wc -l` after each file

Report: files built, TS errors.

Build two features for ISAFlow (/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow).

## Feature 1: Webhook System

Outbound webhooks so integrations can react to ISAFlow events.

### Migration (check next number: `ls scripts/migrations/sql/ | sort | tail -5`)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS webhook_endpoints (
  id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  url         TEXT NOT NULL,
  secret      VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, -- HMAC signing secret
  events      TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- e.g. ['invoice.sent', 'payment.received']
  is_active   BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  created_by  UUID REFERENCES users(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS webhook_deliveries (
  id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  endpoint_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES webhook_endpoints(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  company_id      UUID NOT NULL,
  event_type      VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  payload         JSONB NOT NULL,
  response_status INTEGER,
  response_body   TEXT,
  delivered_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  failed_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
  error_message   TEXT,
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

### Service: `src/modules/accounting/services/webhookService.ts`
```typescript
export const WEBHOOK_EVENTS = [
  'invoice.created', 'invoice.sent', 'invoice.paid', 'invoice.overdue',
  'payment.received', 'payment.confirmed',
  'supplier_invoice.created', 'supplier_invoice.paid',
  'bank_transaction.imported',
] as const;

export type WebhookEvent = typeof WEBHOOK_EVENTS[number];

// Deliver a webhook event to all matching endpoints for a company
export async function deliverWebhook(companyId: string, event: WebhookEvent, payload: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>
// Signs payload with HMAC-SHA256, sends HTTP POST to each active endpoint
// Stores delivery record (success or failure) in webhook_deliveries
// Non-blocking — catches errors, logs but doesn't throw
```

Use Node's built-in `crypto` for HMAC: `import { createHmac } from 'crypto'`
Use `fetch` for HTTP delivery.

### API: `pages/api/accounting/webhooks.ts`
- GET: list webhook endpoints for company
- POST: create endpoint — body: `{ url, secret, events[] }`
  - Validate URL format, events are from WEBHOOK_EVENTS list
- DELETE: `?id=UUID` — delete endpoint

### API: `pages/api/accounting/webhooks-deliveries.ts`
- GET: list recent deliveries `?endpointId=UUID&limit=50`

### Page: `pages/accounting/settings/webhooks.tsx`
- List endpoints with URL, events, active status
- "Add Endpoint" form: URL input, multi-select events checkboxes, secret field (auto-generated)
- "Test" button — sends a `ping` test delivery
- Recent deliveries table (status, event, timestamp)

### Wire delivery into invoice sent event
Find where invoices are marked as 'sent' (likely in customer-invoices-action.ts or similar). After the status update, add:
```typescript
await deliverWebhook(companyId, 'invoice.sent', { invoiceId, invoiceNumber, customerId, totalAmount });
```

## Feature 2: Management Accounts Report Pack

A one-click "Management Accounts" report combining P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow for a selected period.

### API: `pages/api/accounting/reports-management-accounts.ts`
- GET `?fiscalPeriodId=UUID&format=json|pdf`
- Pulls data from existing report services:
  - P&L: aggregate revenue vs expenses GL accounts
  - Balance Sheet: assets, liabilities, equity balances  
  - Cash Flow: bank account movements for the period
- Returns combined JSON structure with all three statements

### Page: `pages/accounting/reports/management-accounts.tsx`
- Period selector (fiscal period dropdown)
- Three collapsible sections: P&L | Balance Sheet | Cash Flow
- KPI summary cards: Revenue, Gross Profit %, Net Profit %, Cash Position
- "Download PDF" button (triggers browser print or PDF endpoint)
- "Email to Director" button (modal with email input)

Add nav entry to reports section.

## Standards
- `withCompany(withErrorHandler(handler as any))`, `withWriteAccess` for mutations
- `sql` tagged templates, company_id scoping on every query
- `apiResponse` helpers, `log` from `@/lib/logger`
- Max 300 lines per file — split if needed
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck 2>&1 | grep "error TS" | wc -l` after each file

# ISAFlow Team Factory

Build and deploy a formal agent team using TeamCreate, TaskCreate, and Agent spawning. Analyzes the input, designs the optimal team, creates tasks, spawns teammates with the right models, and always includes validation agents.

## Trigger

USE WHEN user says "team", "agent team", "spin up a team", "implement this with a team", "team build", "team implement", or provides a PRD/feature doc and wants parallel implementation.

## Workflow — MUST follow this exact sequence

### Step 1: Analyze the Input

Read the input document (PRD, feature list, bug report, or natural language request). Classify it:

| Input Type | Team Shape |
|-----------|------------|
| **PRD** | Full build team (DB + API + UI + validators) |
| **Feature list** | Parallel implementers split by feature + validators |
| **Bug report** | Investigator + fixer + QA |
| **Refactor** | Architect + implementers + validators |
| **Audit** | Auditor + QA + build-check |

### Step 2: Create the Team

Use the `TeamCreate` tool to formally create the team:

```
TeamCreate({
  team_name: "isaflow-{task-slug}",
  description: "Implementing {description of work}",
  agent_type: "team-lead"
})
```

This creates:
- `~/.claude/teams/isaflow-{task-slug}/config.json`
- `~/.claude/tasks/isaflow-{task-slug}/`

### Step 3: Create ALL Tasks Up Front (TDD Order)

Use `TaskCreate` to define every unit of work BEFORE spawning agents.

**ISAFlow enforces Test-Driven Development (TDD). The task order is:**

```
1. TESTS FIRST     → Write failing tests that define expected behavior
2. IMPLEMENTATION  → Write code to make tests pass
3. VALIDATION      → Review, build, browser QA
```

**Phase 1 — Test tasks (created FIRST, no blockers):**
```
TaskCreate({ subject: "Write unit tests for {feature} service", description: "Create tests/unit/{feature}/{feature}Service.test.ts. Write tests for all service functions BEFORE implementation. Tests should define expected inputs/outputs, edge cases, error handling. Use vitest. Tests WILL FAIL initially — that's correct TDD." })
TaskCreate({ subject: "Write API integration tests for {feature}", description: "Create tests/unit/{feature}/{feature}Api.test.ts. Test all API endpoints: valid requests, validation errors, auth checks, company_id scoping. Mock DB responses. Tests WILL FAIL initially." })
TaskCreate({ subject: "Write E2E tests for {feature}", description: "Create tests/e2e/{feature}.spec.ts. Test full user flows: page loads, form submission, data appears in list, navigation works. Use Playwright. Tests WILL FAIL initially." })
```

**Phase 2 — Implementation tasks (blocked by test tasks):**
```
TaskCreate({ subject: "DB migrations for {feature}", description: "Create migration at scripts/migrations/sql/NNN_{name}.sql. Tables need company_id. Use IF NOT EXISTS." })
TaskCreate({ subject: "Service layer for {feature}", description: "Create src/modules/accounting/services/{name}Service.ts. All queries scoped by company_id. Implementation MUST make the unit tests pass." })
TaskCreate({ subject: "API routes for {feature}", description: "Create pages/api/accounting/{name}.ts. Use withCompany(withErrorHandler(handler as any)). Implementation MUST make the API tests pass." })
TaskCreate({ subject: "UI pages for {feature}", description: "Create pages/accounting/{name}/index.tsx and new.tsx. Update accountingNavConfig.ts. Implementation MUST make the E2E tests pass." })
```

**Phase 3 — Validation tasks (blocked by implementation):**
```
TaskCreate({ subject: "Run ALL tests — verify green", description: "Run: bun run test:unit && bun run test:e2e. ALL tests must pass. If any fail, report which tests and why." })
TaskCreate({ subject: "Code review — multi-tenant safety", description: "Check ALL new files for: company_id on queries, withCompany middleware, no console.log, no empty catches, Date object handling, COALESCE(client_id, customer_id) pattern." })
TaskCreate({ subject: "Build validation", description: "Run: bun run build && bunx tsc --noEmit. Report any errors." })
TaskCreate({ subject: "Browser QA — smoke test new pages", description: "Login to https://app.isaflow.co.za (admin@isaflow.co.za / admin123). Test all new pages load, forms submit, nav links work." })
```

**Set TDD dependency chain:**
```
# Implementation blocked by tests (can't code until tests exist)
TaskUpdate({ taskId: "service-impl", addBlockedBy: ["unit-tests"] })
TaskUpdate({ taskId: "api-impl", addBlockedBy: ["api-tests"] })
TaskUpdate({ taskId: "ui-impl", addBlockedBy: ["e2e-tests"] })
TaskUpdate({ taskId: "db-migration", addBlockedBy: ["unit-tests"] })

# Validation blocked by implementation
TaskUpdate({ taskId: "run-tests", addBlockedBy: ["service-impl", "api-impl", "ui-impl"] })
TaskUpdate({ taskId: "code-review", addBlockedBy: ["service-impl", "api-impl", "ui-impl"] })
TaskUpdate({ taskId: "build-check", addBlockedBy: ["service-impl", "api-impl", "ui-impl"] })
TaskUpdate({ taskId: "browser-qa", addBlockedBy: ["build-check"] })
```

### Step 4: Spawn Teammates

Use the `Agent` tool with `team_name` to spawn each teammate. Each gets:
- A `name` (used for SendMessage addressing)
- The right `model` for its task
- `isolation: "worktree"` for implementation agents (avoids file conflicts)
- A clear prompt with ISAFlow rules

**Model routing per role:**

| Role | Phase | Model | Why |
|------|-------|-------|-----|
| test-writer | 1 - Tests | sonnet | Needs to understand business logic to write good tests |
| system-architect | 1 - Tests | opus | Deep reasoning for test strategy on complex PRDs |
| db-architect | 2 - Impl | sonnet | Structured schema work |
| api-builder | 2 - Impl | sonnet | Pattern-following implementation |
| ui-builder | 2 - Impl | sonnet | UI implementation |
| service-builder | 2 - Impl | sonnet | Business logic — must make tests pass |
| test-runner | 3 - Validate | haiku | Runs bun run test:unit, reports pass/fail |
| code-reviewer | 3 - Validate | sonnet | Quality analysis |
| browser-qa | 3 - Validate | sonnet | UI state reasoning via Playwriter |
| build-validator | 3 - Validate | haiku | Just runs commands, checks output |
| security-reviewer | 3 - Validate | opus | Finding vulnerabilities needs depth |
| sage-auditor | 3 - Validate | sonnet | Cross-referencing gap lists |

**TDD Spawning — Phase 1 (Tests First):**
```
Agent({
  name: "test-writer",
  team_name: "isaflow-{task-slug}",
  model: "sonnet",
  isolation: "worktree",
  prompt: "You are test-writer on team isaflow-{task-slug}. TDD: Write tests BEFORE any implementation exists. Create:
    - tests/unit/{feature}/{feature}Service.test.ts (vitest — service logic, edge cases, error handling)
    - tests/unit/{feature}/{feature}Api.test.ts (vitest — API endpoints, validation, auth, company_id scoping)
    - tests/e2e/{feature}.spec.ts (playwright — full user flows)
  Tests MUST fail initially — you are defining the contract. Check TaskList for your test tasks. Mark completed when all test files are written. ISAFlow rules: [include rules from Step 6]",
  run_in_background: true
})
```

**TDD Spawning — Phase 2 (Implementation — after test-writer completes):**
```
Agent({
  name: "service-builder",
  team_name: "isaflow-{task-slug}",
  model: "sonnet",
  isolation: "worktree",
  prompt: "You are service-builder on team isaflow-{task-slug}. TDD: Tests already exist — your job is to make them PASS. Read the test files first to understand the expected behavior, then implement. Run bun run test:unit after each service to verify tests go green. ISAFlow rules: [include rules from Step 6]",
  run_in_background: true
})
```

Spawn ALL Phase 2 agents in a SINGLE message (parallel launch) AFTER Phase 1 completes.

**TDD Spawning — Phase 3 (Validation — after implementation):**
Spawn test-runner + code-reviewer + build-validator + browser-qa after Phase 2.

### Step 5: Coordinate

As team lead:
1. **Monitor** — teammates send messages automatically when done or stuck
2. **Unblock** — when implementation tasks complete, validation tasks auto-unblock
3. **Redirect** — use `SendMessage` to steer agents if they go off track
4. **Merge worktrees** — when implementation agents finish in worktrees, merge their branches
5. **Spawn validators** — after merge, spawn code-reviewer, build-validator, browser-qa
6. **Report** — summarize results to user
7. **Shutdown** — send `{type: "shutdown_request"}` to all teammates, then `TeamDelete`

### Step 6: ISAFlow Rules (inject into EVERY teammate prompt)

```
ISAFlow Critical Rules:
- ALWAYS scope DB queries with company_id (multi-tenant safety)
- ALWAYS use sql tagged templates from @/lib/neon (NEVER string concat)
- ALWAYS wrap API handlers with withCompany(withErrorHandler(handler as any))
- NEVER use console.log — use log from @/lib/logger
- Customer invoices have BOTH client_id AND customer_id — use COALESCE(ci.client_id, ci.customer_id)
- Date columns from Neon return Date objects, not strings — handle both
- Migrations use IF NOT EXISTS on all CREATE TABLE/INDEX
- API responses use apiResponse.success(), .badRequest(), etc. from @/lib/apiResponse
- Package manager is bun (never npm/yarn)
- Max 300 lines per file
- Update accountingNavConfig.ts for any new pages
```

## Team Templates

### PRD Implementation (e.g., "team implement PRD-MIGRATION-WIZARD.md")
```
Phase 1 — Tests:     test-writer(sonnet) writes unit + API + E2E tests
Phase 2 — Implement: db-architect(sonnet) + api-builder(sonnet) + ui-builder(sonnet) [parallel worktrees]
Phase 3 — Validate:  test-runner(haiku) + code-reviewer(sonnet) + build-validator(haiku) + browser-qa(sonnet)

Flow: Tests define contracts → 3 builders make tests pass in parallel → merge → all tests green → validators check
```

### Feature List (e.g., "team fix OUTSTANDING_FEATURES.md")
```
Phase 1 — Tests:     test-writer(sonnet) writes tests for all features
Phase 2 — Implement: N x impl-agent(sonnet) each make their tests pass [parallel worktrees]
Phase 3 — Validate:  test-runner(haiku) + code-reviewer(sonnet) + build-validator(haiku)

Flow: Tests first → split features → each agent codes until their tests pass → merge → validate
```

### Bug Fix (e.g., "team fix invoice PDF broken")
```
Phase 1 — Test:      investigator(sonnet) reproduces bug + writes failing test
Phase 2 — Fix:       fixer(sonnet) makes the test pass
Phase 3 — Validate:  test-runner(haiku) + browser-qa(sonnet)

Flow: Write test that captures the bug → fix it → verify test passes + no regressions
```

### Audit (e.g., "team audit the codebase")
```
No TDD phases — read-only work:
Agents: sage-auditor(sonnet) + code-reviewer(sonnet) + browser-qa(sonnet) — all parallel
Flow: Each audits their dimension → lead synthesizes report
```

### Security Review (e.g., "team security review")
```
Phase 1 — Tests:     test-writer(sonnet) writes security test cases (auth bypass, tenant isolation, injection)
Phase 2 — Audit:     security-reviewer(opus) does deep analysis against those test cases
Phase 3 — Validate:  test-runner(haiku) runs security tests + build-validator(haiku)
```

## Example Execution

User: "team implement the budget module"

What the skill does:
1. `TeamCreate({ team_name: "isaflow-budget", description: "Implement budget module" })`
2. Create 7 tasks (4 implementation + 3 validation) with dependencies
3. Spawn in ONE message:
   - `Agent({ name: "db-architect", team_name: "isaflow-budget", model: "sonnet", isolation: "worktree", prompt: "...", run_in_background: true })`
   - `Agent({ name: "api-builder", team_name: "isaflow-budget", model: "sonnet", isolation: "worktree", prompt: "...", run_in_background: true })`
   - `Agent({ name: "ui-builder", team_name: "isaflow-budget", model: "sonnet", isolation: "worktree", prompt: "...", run_in_background: true })`
4. Wait for implementation agents to complete (auto-notified)
5. Merge worktrees
6. Spawn validators:
   - `Agent({ name: "code-reviewer", team_name: "isaflow-budget", model: "sonnet", prompt: "...", run_in_background: true })`
   - `Agent({ name: "build-validator", team_name: "isaflow-budget", model: "haiku", prompt: "...", run_in_background: true })`
   - `Agent({ name: "browser-qa", team_name: "isaflow-budget", model: "sonnet", prompt: "...", run_in_background: true })`
7. Collect results, report to user
8. `SendMessage({ to: "*", message: { type: "shutdown_request" } })`
9. `TeamDelete()`

- ISAFlow is Next.js 14 + TypeScript strict + Neon PostgreSQL
- Existing items: `pages/api/accounting/items.ts` (read this first to understand the items schema)
- Items are used on invoices, sales orders, purchase orders
- Auth: `withCompany` + `withErrorHandler` middleware  
- DB: `sql` tagged template from `@/lib/neon`
- API responses: `apiResponse.success/created/badRequest/notFound`
- No `console.log` — use `log.info/error` from `@/lib/logger`

### Migration `scripts/migrations/sql/302_item_bundles.sql`
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS item_bundle_lines (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  parent_item_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  child_item_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES items(id),
  quantity NUMERIC(15,4) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  sort_order INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(parent_item_id, child_item_id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_item_bundle_lines_parent ON item_bundle_lines(company_id, parent_item_id);
```

Also: `ALTER TABLE items ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_bundle BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;`

- GET `?itemId=<id>`: return bundle lines for an item (component list)
- POST: add/replace bundle lines for an item (body: `{ item_id, lines: [{ child_item_id, quantity }] }`) — also sets `is_bundle=true` on the parent item
- DELETE `?itemId=<id>`: remove all bundle lines for an item, set `is_bundle=false`

### `pages/api/accounting/items.ts` — extend GET
Add `?expand_bundle=<item_id>` query param: returns the bundle lines with child item details (name, price, unit) for use when auto-expanding on invoice forms.

### `src/components/accounting/items/BundleEditor.tsx`
UI component for editing bundle lines:
- Shows a table of child items with quantity
- Search/add items from company item list
- Remove line button per row
- Save Bundle button
- Used inside the item detail/edit page

### Wire into item detail page

## Standards
- Strict TypeScript, no `any`, no `console.log`
- All queries filter by `company_id`
- Max 300 lines per file
- Run `bunx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep "error TS"` at the end

---
name: frontend-design
description: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
---

This skill guides creation of distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic "AI slop" aesthetics. Implement real working code with exceptional attention to aesthetic details and creative choices.

The user provides frontend requirements: a component, page, application, or interface to build. They may include context about the purpose, audience, or technical constraints.

## Design Thinking

Before coding, understand the context and commit to a BOLD aesthetic direction:
- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?
- **Tone**: Pick an extreme: brutally minimal, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, organic/natural, luxury/refined, playful/toy-like, editorial/magazine, brutalist/raw, art deco/geometric, soft/pastel, industrial/utilitarian, etc. There are so many flavors to choose from. Use these for inspiration but design one that is true to the aesthetic direction.
- **Constraints**: Technical requirements (framework, performance, accessibility).
- **Differentiation**: What makes this UNFORGETTABLE? What's the one thing someone will remember?

**CRITICAL**: Choose a clear conceptual direction and execute it with precision. Bold maximalism and refined minimalism both work - the key is intentionality, not intensity.

Then implement working code (HTML/CSS/JS, React, Vue, etc.) that is:
- Production-grade and functional
- Visually striking and memorable
- Cohesive with a clear aesthetic point-of-view
- Meticulously refined in every detail

## Frontend Aesthetics Guidelines

Focus on:
- **Typography**: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices that elevate the frontend's aesthetics; unexpected, characterful font choices. Pair a distinctive display font with a refined body font.
- **Color & Theme**: Commit to a cohesive aesthetic. Use CSS variables for consistency. Dominant colors with sharp accents outperform timid, evenly-distributed palettes.
- **Motion**: Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Prioritize CSS-only solutions for HTML. Use Motion library for React when available. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions. Use scroll-triggering and hover states that surprise.
- **Spatial Composition**: Unexpected layouts. Asymmetry. Overlap. Diagonal flow. Grid-breaking elements. Generous negative space OR controlled density.
- **Backgrounds & Visual Details**: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Add contextual effects and textures that match the overall aesthetic. Apply creative forms like gradient meshes, noise textures, geometric patterns, layered transparencies, dramatic shadows, decorative borders, custom cursors, and grain overlays.

NEVER use generic AI-generated aesthetics like overused font families (Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts), cliched color schemes (particularly purple gradients on white backgrounds), predictable layouts and component patterns, and cookie-cutter design that lacks context-specific character.

Interpret creatively and make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context. No design should be the same. Vary between light and dark themes, different fonts, different aesthetics. NEVER converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example) across generations.

**IMPORTANT**: Match implementation complexity to the aesthetic vision. Maximalist designs need elaborate code with extensive animations and effects. Minimalist or refined designs need restraint, precision, and careful attention to spacing, typography, and subtle details. Elegance comes from executing the vision well.

Remember: Claude is capable of extraordinary creative work. Don't hold back, show what can truly be created when thinking outside the box and committing fully to a distinctive vision.

# typescript-lsp

TypeScript/JavaScript language server for Claude Code, providing code intelligence features like go-to-definition, find references, and error checking.

## Supported Extensions
`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`

## Installation

Install the TypeScript language server globally via npm:

```bash
npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript
```

Or with yarn:

```bash
yarn global add typescript-language-server typescript
```

## More Information
- [typescript-language-server on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/typescript-language-server)

name: skill-creator
description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, update or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

# Skill Creator

A skill for creating new skills and iteratively improving them.

At a high level, the process of creating a skill goes like this:

- Decide what you want the skill to do and roughly how it should do it
- Write a draft of the skill
- Create a few test prompts and run claude-with-access-to-the-skill on them
- Help the user evaluate the results both qualitatively and quantitatively
  - While the runs happen in the background, draft some quantitative evals if there aren't any (if there are some, you can either use as is or modify if you feel something needs to change about them). Then explain them to the user (or if they already existed, explain the ones that already exist)
  - Use the `eval-viewer/generate_review.py` script to show the user the results for them to look at, and also let them look at the quantitative metrics
- Rewrite the skill based on feedback from the user's evaluation of the results (and also if there are any glaring flaws that become apparent from the quantitative benchmarks)
- Repeat until you're satisfied
- Expand the test set and try again at larger scale

Your job when using this skill is to figure out where the user is in this process and then jump in and help them progress through these stages. You can help narrow down what they mean, write a draft, write the test cases, figure out how they want to evaluate, run all the prompts, and repeat.

On the other hand, maybe they already have a draft of the skill. In this case you can go straight to the eval/iterate part of the loop.

Of course, you should always be flexible and if the user is like "I don't need to run a bunch of evaluations, just vibe with me", you can do that instead.

Then after the skill is done (but again, the order is flexible), you can also run the skill description improver, which we have a whole separate script for, to optimize the triggering of the skill.

Cool? Cool.

## Communicating with the user

The skill creator is liable to be used by people across a wide range of familiarity with coding jargon. If you haven't heard (and how could you, it's only very recently that it started), there's a trend now where the power of Claude is inspiring plumbers to open up their terminals, parents and grandparents to google "how to install npm". tool_input.description: Code quality: transaction safety + Row type cleanup
tool_input.prompt:
Two code quality tasks for ISAFlow — transaction safety and shared DbRow type.

## Task 1: Transaction Safety

Find service files that have multi-step mutations NOT wrapped in a transaction. Focus on these 5 patterns:
1. Create a header record then insert multiple child records (e.g., create order then lines)
2. Update a balance then log an audit entry
3. Delete a parent then delete children (cascade should handle, but verify)
4. Allocate/apply a payment across multiple records
5. Any service that calls `sql` multiple times sequentially where partial failure would leave inconsistent state

Search in `src/modules/accounting/services/` for functions that make 2+ sequential `await sql` calls without using `withTransaction` or `sql.transaction()`.

For each one found:
- Wrap in `withTransaction` from `@/lib/neon` (check its signature — it likely takes a callback with a `TxSql` parameter)
- Pass the `TxSql` through to nested calls
- Keep functions under 300 lines (split if needed)

**Do at most 10 service functions** — prioritise by risk (financial mutations first: payments, allocations, invoices, journal entries).

## Task 2: Shared DbRow Type

Currently ~95 files each declare `type Row = Record<string, unknown>` locally. Create a shared type and replace them.

1. Create `src/types/db.ts`:
```typescript
/** Shared type for raw database row results from Neon sql tagged template. */
export type DbRow = Record<string, unknown>;
```

2. Find all files with `type Row = Record<string, unknown>` — use grep.

3. In each file:
   - Remove the local `type Row = Record<string, unknown>` declaration
   - Add `import type { DbRow } from '@/types/db'`  
   - Replace all `Row` usages with `DbRow` in that file

4. Also handle variants like `type Row = Record<string, unknown>` or similar patterns.

**Do at most 30 files** to stay manageable. Prioritise `src/modules/accounting/services/`.

## Standards
- Strict TypeScript, no `any` introduced
- No `console.log` — use `log.info/error`
- After all changes: run `bunx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep "error TS" | grep -v multiCurrencyService` — must be zero errors
- Max 300 lines per file

Search the codebase first to understand the full scope before making changes.

tool_input.prompt:
Build a Customer Statements page for ISAFlow — a screen where users can view and bulk-email account statements to multiple customers.

## Context
- ISAFlow is Next.js 14 + TypeScript strict + Neon PostgreSQL
- Existing statement APIs: `pages/api/accounting/customer-statements.ts`, `pages/api/accounting/customer-statement.ts`, `pages/api/accounting/customer-statement-detail.ts` — read all three to understand what data is already available
- Email sending: `src/modules/accounting/services/emailService.ts` — has `sendInvoiceEmail` pattern; check how to send arbitrary emails
- Auth: `withCompany` + `withErrorHandler` middleware
- DB: `sql` tagged template from `@/lib/neon`
- No `console.log` — use `log.info/error` from `@/lib/logger`
- Nav: `src/components/accounting/navSections/` — add under Customers or Reports

## What to build

### `pages/api/accounting/customer-statements-send.ts`
POST: Send statements to selected customers
- Body: `{ customer_ids: string[], as_at_date: string, message?: string }`
- For each customer: fetch their statement data, format as email body (HTML table of outstanding invoices with balances), send via emailService
- Return: `{ sent: number, failed: number, errors: string[] }`
- Must have company_id scoping on all queries

### `pages/accounting/statements/index.tsx`
Customer Statements page:
- **Date selector**: "As at date" (defaults to today)
- **Customer list with checkboxes**: show each customer's name, email, outstanding balance, overdue amount
  - Colour-code: red if any overdue, yellow if balance > 0, green if zero
  - "Select All" / "Deselect All" toggle
  - Only show customers with outstanding balance > 0 by default (toggle to show all)
- **Send Statements button**: opens confirmation modal showing count, then POSTs to `/api/accounting/customer-statements-send`
- **Progress feedback**: show sent/failed counts after send completes
- **PDF preview link**: for each customer row, a "Preview" button that opens their statement detail

### Nav wiring
Add "Statements" under Customers section in `src/components/accounting/navSections/`.

## Standards
- Strict TypeScript, no `any`, no `console.log`
- All queries filter by `company_id`
- `withCompany` + `withErrorHandler` on API routes
- Max 300 lines per file — split if needed
- Run `bunx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep "error TS"` at the end

Read all existing statement API files and emailService before writing.

SUMMARY: Four NL-query latency improvements and a per-company sliding-window rate limiter applied to three endpoints.

ANALYSIS:

The original `nl-query.ts` called the Anthropic API with a single flat `user` message containing the full schema + question. This prevented the Anthropic server from caching the large schema block between requests, so every call paid the full TTFT cost. The model was also running at default temperature with 512 max_tokens.

ACTIONS:

**Task 1 — NL Query Performance**

1a. **Prompt caching** — The AI call was restructured from `messages: [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }]` to a proper `system` array with `cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }` on the schema/rules block, and a short `user` turn with only the question + company_id constraint. The `anthropic-beta: prompt-caching-2024-07-31` header is included. Cached tokens (after the first request) are billed at 10% of normal input token cost and, more importantly, are served from Anthropic's KV cache rather than processed by the model — typically saving 200–400ms TTFT on haiku.

1b. **System prompt size** — The old `buildTextToSQLPrompt` stuffed schema + rules + question into one string, with duplicate "CRITICAL" verbiage. The new design pre-builds the system prompt once at module load (`SYSTEM_PROMPT` constant), removing the per-request repetition of the company_id filter from the schema block (it moves to the short user turn). Schema description stayed identical in structure — no content was lost, just restructured.

1c. **Temperature + max_tokens** — `temperature: 0` added (SQL generation is deterministic); `max_tokens` reduced from 512 → 500 (matches the task spec and rounds down the billable token bucket without any practical loss — SQL responses are rarely over 200 tokens).

1d. **In-memory LRU cache** — `queryCache: Map<string, { result, ts }>` at module level, keyed by `companyId + question.toLowerCase()`. Max 100 entries with oldest-entry eviction and 5-minute TTL. Cache hits return immediately, bypassing the AI call, the `withTransaction` DB round-trip, and all prompt processing. Repeat questions (e.g. "what is my revenue this month") are a common real-world pattern.

**Task 2 — API Rate Limiting**

New file `/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow/src/lib/rateLimiter.ts`: pure sliding-window implementation using a `Map<string, number[]>` of request timestamps. On each call, timestamps older than `windowMs` are pruned, then the count is checked against `limit`. Returns `{ allowed, remaining, resetMs }`. Hard cap of 50,000 distinct keys prevents unbounded memory growth. No external dependencies.

Rate limits applied:
- `nl-query.ts` — 20/min per company (`nl-query:${companyId}`)
- `smart-categorize.ts` — 30/min per company (`smart-categorize:${companyId}`)
- `customer-invoices-create.ts` — 60/min per company (`customer-invoices-create:${companyId}`)

All return HTTP 429 with `{ success: false, error: 'Rate limit exceeded', retryAfter: N }`.

RESULTS:

- TypeScript errors: **0** (confirmed by `tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck`)
- Estimated latency improvement:
  - **Prompt caching**: ~200–400ms saved on cached requests (first request cold, subsequent warm)
  - **LRU cache**: ~100% of latency saved on cache hits (no AI or DB call) — applies to identical repeat questions within 5 min
  - **temperature: 0**: marginal (removes sampling randomness, no wall-clock change)
  - **Combined warm-path estimate**: 3.9s → ~0.1s on cache hit; 3.9s → ~3.3–3.5s on cache miss with prompt caching warm

FILES CHANGED:
- `/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow/pages/api/accounting/nl-query.ts` (rewritten)
- `/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow/pages/api/accounting/smart-categorize.ts` (rate limit added)
- `/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow/pages/api/accounting/customer-invoices-create.ts` (rate limit added)
- `/home/hein/Workspace/IsaFlow/src/lib/rateLimiter.ts` (new file)

STATUS: All changes applied, zero TS errors.

NEXT: Deploy and observe Anthropic usage dashboard for `cache_read_input_tokens` to confirm the prompt caching is hitting. If average latency on cache-miss is still above 2s, the remaining candidate is switching from `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` to a smaller/faster model or reducing schema table count to the most-queried subset.

## Context
- ISAFlow is Next.js 14 + TypeScript strict + Neon PostgreSQL
- Existing recurring invoice APIs: `pages/api/accounting/recurring-invoices.ts`, `pages/api/accounting/recurring-invoices-action.ts` — read both to understand the current schema
- Existing recurring transactions: `pages/accounting/recurring-transactions.tsx` — see how recurring transactions are presented
- Email service: `src/modules/accounting/services/emailService.ts`
- Auth: `withCompany` + `withErrorHandler` middleware
- DB: `sql` tagged template from `@/lib/neon`
- No `console.log` — use `log.info/error` from `@/lib/logger`

## What to build

### `pages/accounting/recurring-invoices/index.tsx`
Recurring Invoices management page:
- Table: Customer, Description, Amount, Frequency (monthly/weekly/quarterly), Next Run Date, Last Run Date, Status (active/paused), Actions
- **Run Now** button per row (triggers immediate generation of the next invoice)
- **Pause/Resume** toggle per row
- **Edit** button → edit form
- **New Recurring Invoice** button
- Shows a "Due to run" badge on rows where next_run_date <= today
- **"Run All Due"** button at top to trigger all overdue recurring invoices at once

POST: Run one or all due recurring invoices

- Return: `{ generated: number, invoice_ids: string[], errors: string[] }`
- Must use `withTransaction` for each invoice generation (header + lines atomic)
- Full `company_id` scoping

Create/edit form for a recurring invoice template:

- Auto-send email on generation toggle

- Strict TypeScript, no `any`, no `console.log`
- All queries filter by `company_id`
- `withCompany` + `withErrorHandler` on all API routes
- Max 300 lines per file
- Run `bunx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep "error TS"` at the end

# IsaFlow — CLAUDE.md

## Project

Next.js 14 + TypeScript accounting SaaS. Multi-tenant (every query scoped by `company_id`). Deployed to `app.isaflow.co.za`. Package manager: **bun**.

## Critical Rules (ALL code, ALL agents)

- **Multi-tenant**: ALWAYS add `company_id` to every DB query. Never return data across tenants.
- **DB**: Use `sql` tagged template from `@/lib/neon` — NEVER string concatenation.
- **API handlers**: Wrap with `withCompany(withErrorHandler(handler as any))`.
- **Responses**: Use `apiResponse.success()`, `.badRequest()`, `.notFound()` from `@/lib/apiResponse`.
- **Logging**: Use `log` from `@/lib/logger` — NEVER `console.log`.
- **Error handling**: No empty `catch` blocks.
- **Types**: 100% TypeScript coverage. No `any` except where required by Next.js patterns.
- **File size**: Max 300 lines per file.
- **Dates**: Neon returns `Date` objects — handle both `Date` and `string` shapes.
- **Customer invoices**: Use `COALESCE(ci.client_id, ci.customer_id)` — both columns exist.
- **Nav**: Update `accountingNavConfig.ts` for every new page.
- **Migrations**: `IF NOT EXISTS` on all `CREATE TABLE` / `CREATE INDEX`.

## Key Paths

| What | Where |
|------|-------|
| DB client | `src/lib/neon.ts` |
| API response helpers | `src/lib/apiResponse.ts` |
| Logger | `src/lib/logger.ts` |
| Auth middleware | `src/lib/withCompany.ts` |
| Services | `src/modules/accounting/services/` |
| API routes | `pages/api/accounting/` |
| UI pages | `pages/accounting/` |
| Migrations | `scripts/migrations/sql/` |
| Nav config | `src/components/layout/accountingNavConfig.ts` |
| Unit tests | `tests/unit/` |
| E2E tests | `tests/e2e/` |

## Commands

```bash
bun run dev          # Start dev server
bun run build        # Production build
bun run test:unit    # Vitest unit tests
bunx tsc --noEmit    # Type check
bash scripts/deploy.sh  # Deploy
```

## Testing

- Unit tests: Vitest in `tests/unit/services/`
- E2E: Playwright in `tests/e2e/`
- TDD enforced: tests FIRST, implementation second

## Plugins Active

- `/frontend-design` — bold/distinctive UI components (avoid generic AI aesthetics)
- `/superpowers` — git worktrees, TDD, parallel agents, debugging
- `context7` MCP — fetch live docs for Next.js, React, Neon, etc.
- `/code-review` — multi-agent PR code review
- `github` MCP — GitHub API (requires `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`)
- `/skill-creator` — create/iterate new skills
- `/revise-claude-md` — update this file after sessions
- `typescript-lsp` — TS go-to-def, find-references, error checking
- `/review-pr` — comprehensive PR review with specialized agents
- `telegram` MCP — Telegram notifications (deploy alerts, etc.)
